sections.h2: Visiting or contacting the Shelby office
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is in Room 151 of the county administration building, 311 E. Marion Street, Shelby, NC 28150. It is open weekdays from eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, and the land records line is 704-484-4834. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1210, Shelby, NC 28151, and email to rod.info@clevelandcountync.gov, as the office's frequently asked questions page lists.

Everything on file is public except military discharge records. Passports, marriage licenses (by appointment) and certified vital records go through the same counter, so expect a mixed crowd.

Owners live in most Cleveland County homes: about 70.9 percent of occupied homes, with a median value of $200,000 for 2020 to 2024. The county has roughly 103,325 residents.

sections.h2: What the office records and how to submit
sections.html:
The office records the paperwork that moves or secures a house. It accepts paper, overnight courier and electronic submissions. The land record recordings page lists the documents it files.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust
  • Easements and powers of attorney
  • Satisfactions of paid loans
  • Plats, accepted by e-recording since 2019
  • Assumed business name certificates
  • Notary oaths, by appointment only

Electronic filers use Simplifile, CSC or ePN. Send an original by courier with a prepaid return envelope and the recorded document comes back in it, and there is no extra charge to schedule a FedEx pickup. Wills are not recorded here; they go to the Clerk of Court.

A filing costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each page after that. Mortgage-type documents get a longer first block under the state fee statute: 35 pages for $64.00.

  • Copies of deeds in person: $.25 per page.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for every page after it.
  • Assumed business name certificate: $26.00 to record, plus a $15.00 vendor convenience fee if filed online, for $41.00 through the online portal.
  • Transfer tax on a sale: $2.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price.

To put a new name on a title, have a new deed drawn up by an attorney. Staff record deeds but do not draft them.

The seller does, and the register collects it before filing. The state statute sets it at $1.00 per $500.00 of consideration or value, with any leftover fraction counted as a full $500.00, which equals the office's per-thousand wording.

Half of the money stays in the county general fund. The other half, minus refunds and the county's allowance, moves on to the state. At a closing the attorney usually deducts it from your proceeds, so you see a deduction on the settlement statement instead of a bill at the counter.

sections.h2: Searching Cleveland County land records online
sections.html:
Verified online records start in 1995. Older material sits in an unverified index and in scanned index books. The available land records page gives the ranges.

Online coverage of Cleveland County land records
Record setDates covered
Searchable real property index01/03/1995 to present
New unverified searchable index01/01/1945 to 12/31/1994
Searchable plat index (starts with Plat Book 19)05/16/1995 to present
Viewable images of index books1841 to 1944

Entries from 1979 to 1985 can be searched only by name and year, so open the document to see the exact recording date. Images from before 1960 need the book and page number, and a book such as 15-A is typed as 15A with no dash. Anything not online can be viewed at the office, which also offers escrow accounts for faxed or emailed copies for a fee.

Some residents receive a solicitation that looks like a bill. The register of deeds warns people not to pay it. The mailer asks for $86.00 for a "Property Assessment Profile" that includes a copy of your deed.

The same documents cost 25 cents per page from the Cleveland County Mapping Office and the Register of Deeds. Report the notice to the Consumer Protection Division of the N.C. Department of Justice at 919-716-6000. The office also runs a fraud detection notification service. After you sign up, check your spam folder for the confirmation email and confirm it.

If a relative is selling or has inherited a house in the county, pass this warning along.

The register of deeds keeps recorded plats only. Every other map comes from the Cleveland County Mapping Office at 704-484-4849, which also answers parcel questions by street address.

If you plan to divide a lot, call the register before filing. The office points e-recording filers to it for the review officer and administrator signatures that plats need.

Two situations call for extra paperwork before the register can act. After a death, G.S. 28A-25-1 lets an heir, creditor or public administrator use an affidavit in place of a full estate once 30 days have gone by and personal property net of liens is $20,000 or less. The affidavit goes to the court clerk and describes every tract of real property the decedent owned.

A seller who finances a one to four family home through a contract for deed must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days under Chapter 47H. The buyer has until midnight on the third business day to cancel. Both tasks end at the Shelby counter. If a house is stuck in probate or needs repairs before a sale, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale route.

Tax Administration shares the building at 311 East Marion Street and answers at 704-484-4843. Bring questions about the bill on the parcel you just sold to that office.

Bills are due each September 1 and carry interest from January 6 (G.S. 105-360), so make sure your settlement agent knows what has been paid. Recording is a separate step, and G.S. 47-18 ranks instruments by who registers first where the parcel sits. The deed belongs at the Shelby counter the day you close.

If you file yourself rather than through an attorney, send the original with payment for the $26.00 first block of pages and the transfer tax. A prepaid return envelope brings the recorded deed back to you. Call 704-484-4834 first if you are unsure what your document needs, since staff can explain fees but cannot draft or correct it.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Cleveland County deed office?
faqs.a: Weekdays from eight to five, in Room 151 at 311 E. Marion Street, Shelby. Call 704-484-4834 about land records.

faqs.q: Does the Shelby office accept electronic filings?
faqs.a: Yes. It e-records through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and has taken plats electronically since 2019. Overnight courier recordings are also accepted at the Shelby address.

faqs.q: What is the price of filing a deed in Shelby?
faqs.a: $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 for each added page. A sale also carries transfer tax, which the office puts at $2.00 per thousand dollars of the price.

faqs.q: Are wills filed with the Cleveland County deed office?
faqs.a: No. Wills go to the Clerk of Court. Deeds, easements, plats, loan documents and payoff satisfactions go to the register.

faqs.q: What do I do with an $86.00 deed notice that looks like a bill?
faqs.a: Do not pay it. The register says the property profile is available for 25 cents a page, and it asks you to report the mailer to the Consumer Protection Division at the N.C. Department of Justice.
